official.description: The Walczak NAWA Programme is named after Professor Franciszek Walczak, who headed the Cardiac Rhythm Disorders Clinic at the Institute of Cardiology in Anin, performed the first RF ablation in Poland in an adult in 1992 and in a child in 1994, and is considered a doyen of Polish electrophysiology. The programme aims to strengthen the potential of Polish scientific units and medical entities by supporting the international mobility of researchers in medical sciences, pharmaceutical sciences and health sciences. So far, thanks to the commitment of the Ministry of Health, three calls have been settled, awarding grants for travel to the best medical centres in the United States to 57 people for a total of PLN 4 299 000. With the substantive support of the Medical Research Agency, the new edition opens the programme to the entire world, so that not only representatives of medical sciences but also those in pharmaceutical and health sciences can apply.
official.program_type: Government outbound research mobility programme in medical and health sciences

applicant_utility.summary: Walczak is an outbound mobility award, not a degree scholarship: you keep your post and travel to a foreign medical centre for one to six months, choosing between a teaching, research or clinical track, with up to PLN 32,000 per month of stay covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel. If you are a doctoral student or researcher on the scientific path and can stay longer than three months, you can also claim a one-off PLN 20,000. Eligibility is specifically for medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences, so a social science or humanities applicant will not fit. There is currently no open call: the only announcement on NAWA's pages is no. 41/2024 of 5 December 2024, and the programme page's reference to a call running until 31 January 2024 is out of date, so watch NAWA's Walczak pages rather than assuming a fixed annual round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Polish doctor, doctoral student or academic teacher in medical, pharmaceutical or health sciences with a host invitation from a foreign medical centre and a one-to-six month development plan.

Planning a stay of less than three months and expecting the PLN 20 000 material support, which requires the scientific path and a longer stay

A diploma of participation at the end of the programme, following preparation and defence of a diploma paper of scientific or practical character

Final results are sent by email by the end of May or in June, and candidates selected to take part have the opportunity to take a language exam organized in mid-June

Rewarded characteristics include candidates active in their professional and social communities, candidates with significant achievements, candidates who have not studied in Poland so far, and candidates who opt for studies in Polish

official.application_route: Apply online through the programme administration form linked from the programme website, with all documents submitted electronically; the form must be registered for the application to be valid, and contact for administrative problems is kirkland@kirkland.edu.pl.
official.study_mode: Full-time, two-semester non-degree study programme at a Polish university, plus a professional internship
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship and permanent residence in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Tajikistan, Ukraine or Uzbekistan; holders of a residence card in Poland and people living or working in Poland when applying are ineligible.
official.international_eligibility: Open only to nationals of the listed countries who are not resident in Poland; residence in Poland at the time of application, and enrolment at a Polish institution during the selection process, both make a candidate ineligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Fields available to grantees are limited to areas related to systemic and economic transformation: economics and management, business and NGO management, public administration, law, social sciences, political science and journalism, development policy and humanitarian aid, environmental protection, security issues and crisis management.
official.duration: Two semesters of studies, from the introductory course in the second half of September to the graduation ceremony at the end of the following June, plus an internship of at least two weeks
official.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program has been supporting individual development of young, ambitious and active citizens of Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus and Central Asia for over two decades, and more than 1,000 graduates have taken part since 2000. The author and founder of the program is the Polish-American Freedom Foundation, and the programme is also supported financially by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange. It is run by the Leaders of Change Foundation as administrator, from the Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program Office in Warsaw. The programme offers two semesters of studies at one of four Polish academic centers, Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw and Lublin, a professional internship of at least two weeks, and an extensive training and workshop programme, and is addressed to young leaders and experts interested in the development of democracy, economy and civil society in their countries and the region.
official.program_type: Foundation-administered postgraduate non-degree study scholarship with Polish government support
official.english_requirement: B2 in the language of study, Polish or English. Candidates studying in English must also have Polish at A1 level; candidates from Belarus and Ukraine have retained their eligibility, though study.gov.pl records that studies in English are not possible for candidates from Belarus and Ukraine.

applicant_utility.summary: Kirkland is a long-running leadership programme rather than a degree: two semesters of non-degree study at a Polish university in Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw or Lublin, an internship of at least two weeks, and a PLN 22,500 stipend paid over nine months, with accommodation, insurance, travel, transport, visa costs, materials and a Polish language course provided on top, which the administrator values at about PLN 5,000 a month. The decisive part of the application is the project statement of 4,000 to 6,000 characters, which the experts read first. You need at least two years of professional experience, a completed degree, and two years clear of any previous foreign scholarship longer than six months; living in Poland now disqualifies you outright, and candidates from Belarus and Ukraine cannot study in English under the current rules. Applications close on 1 March, and the results only come by email at the end of May or in June, so this is a programme to apply for a full year ahead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A mid-career professional, civil servant, lawyer, entrepreneur, NGO or media leader, academic teacher or journalist aged under 40 with at least two years of professional experience and a concrete plan to translate the Polish transition experience back home.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you have not lived in Poland during the selection process and have not previously attended a Polish university, both of which disqualify
Confirm two years of professional experience, and gather employment history even though certificates from workplaces are not required
Decide between studies in Polish and studies in English, and if English, identify the specific programme and city in advance
Draft the project statement to the 4,000-6,000 character range and register the form only once it is complete, since registration fixes the data
Obtain two reference letters in Polish or English that are not written by family members or life partners
Scan your diploma and have it ready electronically; nothing should be sent by regular post
common_rejection_risks: Under-running the project statement below 4,000 characters, which prevents the form from registering at all
Holding a recent foreign scholarship longer than six months within the last two years, or studying in Poland during the selection
Being a current student, since the programme requires a completed diploma at the time of application
Expecting to negotiate the language level in the interview: candidates weak in Polish but strong in content may take the mid-June language exam, and the result decides qualification
Writing a project statement that is generic rather than tied to a proposed programme, city and internship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everyday living expenses beyond the stipend and the provided package, and any costs of the internship beyond what the programme administers. The programme is also non-degree, so there is no tuition saving to count against a future degree.
document_audit: The project statement must reach 4,000 characters with spaces; a shorter statement silently blocks registration of the form
Reference letters must be sent electronically and must not come from family members or life partners
Only the form registered and submitted electronically counts; the programme warns that nothing should be sent by regular post
alerts: The programme does not provide individual feedback on unsuccessful applications
Candidates who pass qualification but not the language exam in June may still be admitted after taking the exam
The Kirkland Research Program runs in parallel for PhD holders, with a stipend of PLN 10,800 in 4 instalments and a one-semester research stay, and requires at least four years of research experience

The programme is run by an independent foundation, the Leaders of Change Foundation, on behalf of the Polish-American Freedom Foundation, so the application channel is the programme's own form and not the NAWA system
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete and register the online application form on the programme's website during the annual window that closes on 1 March, with the project statement, motivation statement, two electronic reference letters and a scanned diploma. Final results are sent by email.
